description: A feature the system must provide, such as "users can shorten a URL" or "a short URL redirects to the original".
A quality the system must have: availability, latency, consistency, durability or security, ideally with a number attached.
Daily active users, requests per user, read/write ratio and retention: the inputs that turn a vague prompt into capacity targets.
Explicit agreement on the high-level design before the deep dive, so detailed work goes into the parts that matter.
Detailed design of the two or three components that carry the hard problems, chosen from the requirements.
What a choice gains and what it costs, stated against a requirement: option, benefit, cost, choice.
The closing step: bottlenecks, failure modes and next steps for the design you proposed.
